strings.name: Elif Shafak
strings.summary: Writing in Turkish and English, Shafak explores gender and cultural plurality through family memory, migration and cities. The Bastard of Istanbul led to prosecution, followed by acquittal in 2006; 10 Minutes 38 Seconds reached the Booker shortlist. Later novels traverse Cyprus, river histories and Flaubert's world, alongside her advocacy for free expression.

strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Strasbourg, France; grew up mainly in Turkey and several other countries.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied international relations, women's studies and political science at Middle East Technical University; earned a political-science PhD.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Connecting literary cultures
strings.highlights.h1.text: Uses multiple voices to portray Istanbul, migration and different cultural memories.
strings.highlights.h2.title: The overlooked in fiction
strings.highlights.h2.text: Brings women, minorities and historically marginalized people into her narratives.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Published a Flaubert novel
strings.timeline.t1.text: In One Brief Moment All Eternity retells the writer's life through women and fictional characters.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Literary society presidency
strings.timeline.t2.text: Was appointed president of the Royal Society of Literature, continuing her public literary work.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Published a river novel
strings.timeline.t3.text: There Are Rivers in the Sky connects the Thames, the Tigris and memory.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Published The Island of Missing Trees
strings.timeline.t4.text: Explored division and migration through family and natural memory in Cyprus.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Booker shortlist
strings.timeline.t5.text: 10 Minutes 38 Seconds in This Strange World was shortlisted.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Published The Forty Rules of Love
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joined contemporary and historical narratives of love, faith and Rumi's world.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Prosecution and acquittal
strings.timeline.t7.text: The Bastard of Istanbul addressed Armenian history; she was prosecuted and acquitted that year.
